 THURSDAY ,THE TWELFTH DAY OF DECEMBER  TWO THOUSAND AND TWENTY FOUR  PRESENT  THE HONOURABLE SRI JUSTICE NYAPATHY VIJAY  CIVIL MISCELLANEOUS APPEAL NO: 777/2024 Between:
The New India Assurance Company Ltd., ...APPELLANT  AND Smt Sadineni Sarala And 5 Others ...RESPONDENT Counsel for the Appellant:
1. AMANCHARLA SATISH BABU Counsel for the Respondent:

1. 
The Court made the following:
 THE HON'BLE SRI JUSTICE NYAPATHY VIJAY  C.M.A No.777 of 2024 JUDGMENT:
The present appeal is filed under section 30 of the Employees Compensation Act, questioning the order dated31.10.2012 in W.C.No.25 of 2007 passed by the Commissioner for Workmen's Compensation and Assistant Commissioner of Labour, Guntur.
2.

The facts leading to this appeal are as under:
The O.P.No.1 is the registered owner of the car bearing No. AP 37W 2648.

The O.P.No.2 is also the owner of the same Car as the same transferred from O.P.No.1 The New India Assurance Company Ltd., vs Smt. Sadineni Sarala And 5 Others on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/159731556/
1 and O.P.No.3 is the insurance company.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On 14.09.2006, at about 8.30 p.m., the workman late Sadineni Ramanjaneyalu, who was working as Driver under O.P.No.2 was on duty in the car bearing No. AP 37 W 2648 going from Guntur to Tirumala.

As he did not return after his duty, a complaint was filed in Kothapeta Police Station,
Guntur and a case in Cr.No.596 of 2006 was registered.
On 19.09.2006 the dead body of the deceased was found near bridge, bye pass road, Nellore by the road security officer and another Cr.No.249 of 2006 was registered by Nellore Rural P.S.
The claimants being the wife, daughter and parents of the deceased workman filed the claim petition seeking compensation of Rs.4,00,000/- from the opposite parties.

5. The insurance company filed their counter denying that though the vehicle was transferred from O.P.No.1 to O.P.No.2, the policy with regard to the same was not transferred and hence, the insurance company is not liable to pay compensation as there is no privity of contract between opposite party No.2 and the insurance company.
6.
The O.P.Nos.1 and 2 remained ex parte and insurance company i.e., opposite party No.3 filed counter denying any responsibility.
It was pleaded that the deceased did not sustain any injuries in the course of employment and the death cannot be related to the employment.
The further defence was that the Insurance Policy for the vehicle bearing No. AP 37 W 2468 was given to one M.Ramesh Babu and not in favour of O.P.No.2.
As there is no employer-employee relationship between M.Ramesh Babu and deceased, no liability can be fastened on the Insurance Company.
7. The wife of the deceased examined as A.W.1 and Exs.A.1 to A.11 were marked while the Insurance Company got marked Exs.B.1 to B.2 and B.W.1 was examined.

8. The commissioner framed four issues for consideration:
1. Whether the deceased sadineni Ramanjaneyulu was a workman U/S.2(1)(n) of the Workmen S Compensation Act at the time of his death?
And whether the deceased had died as a result of incident arising out of and in the course of employment?
2. If so, what is the wage and age of the deceased at the time of his death?
3. What is the amount of compensation?
4. Who are liable to pay compensation to the dependants of the deceased?

8. The Commissioner after taking into consideration the respective contentions directed O.P.No.2 and the insurance company to pay compensation of Rs.3,44,604/-
jointly and severally.

The Commissioner relied on Ex.A.3 charge sheet wherein it was stated that the deceased was murdered while on duty a driver of the vehicle on 14.09.2006, and held that the death of the deceased was in the course of The New India Assurance Company Ltd., vs Smt. Sadineni Sarala And 5 Others on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/159731556/
2 employment.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As regards the plea of transfer of the vehicle, the Commissioner noted that no such transfer was effected in the office of Regional Transport Officer and held the Insurance Company liable.
Hence, the present appeal is filed.

9. Heard Sri Amancharla Satish Babu, learned counsel for the appellant and Sri Rajendra Babu, learned counsel for the respondents.
10.
The only issue urged by the counsel for the appellant is that the insurance company is not liable for the amounts as there was no transfer of policy.

The counsel for the respondents contended that though the policy did not actually transfer in favour of O.P.No.2, the insurance company is liable to pay compensation as the statutory contract of indemnity being a statutory requirement and the same is for the compensation arising out of accident caused by the vehicle irrespective of the owner.
11.

The only question that falls for consideration in this appeal is, whether the Commissioner was correct in holding the Insurance Company liable in the absence of transfer of Policy in favour of O.P.No.2?
12.

The evidence on record does not show transfer of ownership as required under Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 and this defence was based on charge sheet EX.A.3.
13.
Though the claimants submitted that the deceased worked under the employment of the O.P.2, the O.P.No.1 is the owner of the vehicle.

The Insurance Company which had taken the defence of lack of employer-employee relationship by taking clue from the claim itself should have summoned O.P.No.1 and examined him to establish that there was no employer-employee relationship.
The claimants being ignorant of the arrangement between O.P.No.1 and O.P.No.2, cannot be expected to explain as to who was employer of the deceased.

The deceased was undisputedly murdered while on duty as driver of vehicle owned by O.P.1 and therefore, notwithstanding the admission that O.P.No.2 was the employer of the deceased, the O.P.No.1 alone has to be taken as the employer of the deceased.
The statement by the claimants regarding O.P.No.2 as employer is clearly erroneous.
Innocent admission on incorrect understanding of the illiterate and ignorant claimants cannot be basis to exonerate the liability of the insurance company.
14. Notwithstanding the above, even if the vehicle is transferred to O.P.No.2, the liability of the Insurance Company shall not cease.

This issue was considered by Hon'ble Supreme Court in Firdaus v. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd.,1and at paragraphs 12 and 15 thereof, it is held as under:
"12.

entities.text: Firdaus v. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Even if it is assumed for the sake of arguments that vehicle was transferred from Defendant 1 to Defendant 4, there will be no consequence with regard to liability of Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. to pay the compensation.

The issue has been answered in Rikhi Ram case [Rikhi Ram v. Sukhrania, (2003) 3 SCC 97 : 2003 SCC (Cri) 735]

sentences.text:
The vehicle involved in the accident in the aforesaid case was insured by another owner, namely,
M/s Bhagwan Rai Amrit Lal, which was purchased by two other persons subsequently.
No intimation of transfer was given to Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd.

The question arose in the above case,
as to whether in the absence of intimation of transfer to the insurer the liability to pay the compensation to the third party shall cease.
This Court held that even if vehicle stand transferred to the name of another person, the liability of insurer to pay compensation to third party shall not cease........."
"15. In view of the above, it is not necessary for us to give any concluded finding regarding ownership of Vehicle No. HR 2 G 1875 on the date of accident for the purpose of this case.
In either of the eventuality i.e. whether Defendant 1 was the owner of the vehicle on the date of the accident, or Defendant 4 was the owner of the vehicle
, the liability of Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. continues and the Workmen Compensation Commissioner has rightly fastened the liability on the (2017) 15 SCC 674 Insurance Company.
The remand made by the High Court to find out as to whether Parvez Khan was an employee of Defendant 1 or not, was unnecessary."
15. Therefore, this Court does not find any substantial question of law in the appeal and the civil miscellaneous appeal is dismissed.
16. The State Legal Services Authority shall ensure that the compensation is paid to the claimants directly into their Aadhar linked Bank account.
No order as to costs.
As a sequel, the miscellaneous petitions, if any, shall stand closed.
